function: Distributed downlink beamforming: a GNN outputs each AP-UE link's beamformer, minimizing the worst user's decoding error probability under per-AP power limits in URLLC (p. 5, p. 6).
system: Downlink cell-free massive MIMO: 10 APs with 8 antennas each, 6 single-antenna UEs, up to 4 serving APs per UE, 2.4 GHz carrier; no RIS (p. 3, p. 11).
method: GNN with per-link FNNs for message, update, output; G4PCF single layer reusing previous-frame embedding; P-G4PCF parallel variant; unsupervised offline training, Adam, min-SINR loss (p. 7, p. 10, p. 11).
data_channel: Synthetic: 2x10^3 training and 2x10^3 test layouts, 10 frames; ITU-R P.1411 path loss, 3 dB shadowing, i.i.d. Rayleigh fading with Gauss-Markov correlation 0.99 (p. 4, p. 11).
test_conditions: Trained with K=6 UEs, M=10 APs (p. 11); tested on new layouts, and for scalability with 6-14 UEs, 12-20 APs, frame duration 0.1-0.7 ms (p. 13, p. 14); rho=0.99.
baselines: Classical: WMMSE (20 iterations, overhead and delay ignored). Learned: only the paper's own GNN variants G4CF, P-G4CF; no earlier learned method simulated (p. 11).
metrics: Training and test loss, worst-UE URLLC rate in bit/s/Hz, QoS outage probability Pr(DEP > 1e-7), signaling overhead and computation delay (p. 12, p. 13).
complexity: Computation delay Tc=3tc (3 FNN executions per frame) for G4PCF, 0 for P-G4PCF versus 2(N+1)tc for a conventional GNN; tc=100 us assumed, not measured (p. 10, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "temporally correlated Rayleigh fading channels"; p. 11: "the large-scale fading gains are modeled using the following propagation model [39]" (ITU-R P.1411 path loss only); custom simulator, no 3GPP or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "with K = 6 UEs and M = 10 APs in each layout"; p. 12: "We now test the scalability of the trained GNN models"; p. 13: "as a function of the number of UEs" (6-14 UEs, 12-20 APs in Figs. 10-11).
q3_support: p. 11: "alongside the classical WMMSE algorithm [25], [40], [41]"; p. 10: "the technical frameworks in fully connected network are named by G4CF and P-G4CF", own variants; no earlier learned method simulated.
q4_support: p. 9: "The total computation delay for G4PCF is expressed as" Tc = 3tc; Table I on p. 10; p. 12: "computation delay for the proposed G4PCF framework are 76.8 µs and 300 µs, respectively".
q5_support: p. 11: "layouts are randomly generated"; synthetic layouts and channels, no code or data link and no public dataset in the paper.
notes: Area 3: the GNN outputs per-AP beamformers, while the AP-UE association is fixed (p. 11: half of the APs serve the UEs). q1: path loss follows ITU-R P.1411 (p. 11) but fading is custom Rayleigh, treated like path loss only from a standard, so 0; reviewer may confirm. q2 is 1 because the trained models are tested with more UEs and APs than in training (pp. 11-13), but the paper does not say whether each size was retrained. q3: only WMMSE and the authors' own variants are compared. q4 is borderline: computation delay counts FNN executions with an assumed tc, with no FLOPs, parameters or measured runtime.
